scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with an iceberg. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 101 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. A protective barrier on the boat is currently keeping 10 of the passengers from falling over. However, the ocean water is extremely cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly freeze to death.
choice: I decide to remove the barrier protecting 10 passengers from falling overboard
entities: I,other crew members and passengers in Lifeboat A,10 passengers protected by the barrier on Lifeboat B,91 other passengers and crew members on Lifeboat B
outcomes: 10 passengers in Lifeboat B fall into the freezing ocean
91 passengers and crew in Lifeboat B remain in a boat that no longer faces immediate sinking from overcrowding
The other survivors and I witness the passengers falling overboard and experience shock and distress
